stories.title: 🌿 Geremia 1
summaryBullets: Parole di Geremia, figlio di Chilchia, uno dei sacerdoti che stavano ad Anatot, nel paese di Beniamino. (1:1).
La parola del Signore gli fu rivolta al tempo di Giosia, figlio di Amon, re di Giuda, l’anno tredicesimo del suo regno, (1:2).

e al tempo di Ieoiachim, figlio di Giosia, re di Giuda, sino alla fine dell’anno undicesimo di Sedechia, figlio di Giosia, re di Giuda, fino a quando Gerusalemme fu deportata, il che avvenne nel quinto mese. (1:3).
The word of il SIGNORE came to Jeremiah, saying (1:4),
«Prima che io ti avessi formato nel grembo di tua madre, io ti ho conosciuto; prima che tu uscissi dal suo grembo, io ti ho consacrato e ti ho costituito profeta delle nazioni». (1:5).
Then Jeremiah said, "Ah, Lord GOD! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth" (1:6).
Ma il Signore mi disse: «Non dire: “Sono un ragazzo”, perché tu andrai da tutti quelli ai quali ti manderò e dirai tutto quello che io ti comanderò. (1:7).
"Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you," declares il SIGNORE (1:8).
Then il SIGNORE put out his hand and touched Jeremiah's mouth and said, "Behold, I have put my words in your mouth" (1:9).
"See, I have set you this day over nations and over kingdoms, to pluck up and to break down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant" (1:10).
And the word of il SIGNORE came to Jeremiah, saying, "What do you see?" And he said, "I see an almond branch" (1:11).
Then il SIGNORE said, "You have seen well, for I am watching over my word to perform it" (1:12).
La parola del Signore mi fu rivolta per la seconda volta: «Che cosa vedi?» Io risposi: «Vedo una gran pentola che bolle e ha la bocca rivolta dal settentrione in qua». (1:13).
E il Signore mi disse: «Dal settentrione verrà fuori la calamità su tutti gli abitanti del paese. (1:14).

Poiché, ecco, io sto per chiamare tutti i popoli dei regni del settentrione», dice il Signore; «essi verranno e porranno ognuno il suo trono all’ingresso delle porte di Gerusalemme, contro tutte le sue mura all’intorno e contro tutte le città di Giuda. (1:15).
"And I will declare my judgments against them, for all their evil in forsaking me; they have made offerings to other gods and worshiped the works of their own hands" (1:16).
"But you, dress yourself for work; arise, and say to them everything that I command you. Do not be dismayed by them, lest I dismay you before them" (1:17).

Ecco, oggi io ti stabilisco come una città fortificata, come una colonna di ferro e come un muro di bronzo contro tutto il paese, contro i re di Giuda, contro i suoi prìncipi, contro i suoi sacerdoti e contro il popolo del paese. (1:18).
"They will fight against you, but they shall not prevail against you, for I am with you," declares il SIGNORE, "to deliver you" (1:19).

stories.title: 💧 Geremia 2
summaryBullets: The word of il SIGNORE came to Jeremiah, saying (2:1),

«Va’, e grida alle orecchie di Gerusalemme: “Così dice il Signore: ‘Io mi ricordo dell’affetto che avevi per me quand’eri giovane, del tuo amore da fidanzata, quando mi seguivi nel deserto, in una terra non seminata. (2:2).
Israel was holy to il SIGNORE, the firstfruits of his harvest; all who ate of it incurred guilt, and disaster came upon them, declares il SIGNORE (2:3).
Ascoltate la parola del Signore, o casa di Giacobbe, e voi tutte le famiglie della casa d’Israele! (2:4).
"What wrong did your fathers find in me that they went far from me, and went after worthlessness, and became worthless?" (2:5).

They did not say, "Where is il SIGNORE who brought us up from il paese d’Egitto, who led us in the wilderness, in a land of deserts and pits, in a land of drought and deep darkness, in a land that none passes through?" (2:6).
God brought them into a plentiful land to enjoy its fruits and its good things, but when they came in, they defiled the land and made God's heritage an abomination (2:7).

The priests did not say, "Where is il SIGNORE?" Those who handle the law did not know God; the shepherds transgressed, and the prophets prophesied by Baal and went after things that do not profit (2:8).
"Therefore I still contend with you," declares il SIGNORE, "and with your children's children I will contend" (2:9).
"Cross to the coasts of Cyprus and see, or send to Kedar and examine with care; see if there has been such a thing" (2:10).
"Has a nation changed its gods, even though they are no gods? But my people have changed their glory for that which does not profit" (2:11).
"Be appalled, O heavens, at this; be shocked, be utterly desolate," declares il SIGNORE (2:12).
"For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living waters, and hewed out cisterns for themselves, broken cisterns that can hold no water" (2:13).
"Is Israel a slave? Is he a homeborn servant? Why then has he become a prey?" (2:14).
The young lions have roared against him; they have roared loudly. They have made his land a waste; his cities are in ruins, without inhabitant (2:15).
Moreover, the men of Memphis and Tahpanhes have shaved the crown of your head (2:16).
"Have you not brought this upon yourself by forsaking il SIGNORE your God, when he led you in the way?" (2:17).
E ora, perché vai per la via che conduce in Egitto per andare a bere l’acqua del Nilo? O perché vai per la via che conduce in Assiria per andare a bere l’acqua dell’Eufrate? (2:18).

Your evil will discipline you, and your apostasy will reprove you. Know and see that it is evil and bitter for you to forsake il SIGNORE your God; the fear of me is not in you, declares the Lord GOD of hosts (2:19).
"Long ago you broke your yoke and burst your bonds; you said, 'I will not serve.' For on every high hill and under every green tree you bowed down like a whore" (2:20).
"Yet I planted you a choice vine, wholly of pure seed. How then have you turned degenerate and become a wild vine?" (2:21).
"Though you wash yourself with lye and use much soap, the stain of your guilt is still before me," declares the Lord GOD (2:22).
"How can you say, 'I am not unclean, I have not gone after the Baals'? Look at your way in the valley; know what you have done—a restless young camel running here and there" (2:23).
"A wild donkey used to the wilderness, in her heat sniffing the wind! Who can restrain her lust? None who seek her need weary themselves; in her month they will find her" (2:24).
"Keep your feet from going unshod and your throat from thirst. But you said, 'It is hopeless, for I have loved foreigners, and after them I will go'" (2:25).
Come il ladro è confuso quand’è colto sul fatto, così sono confusi quelli della casa d’Israele: essi, i loro re, i loro capi, i loro sacerdoti e i loro profeti, (2:26).

They say to a tree, "You are my father," and to a stone, "You gave me birth." For they have turned their back to God and not their face, but in the time of their trouble they say, "Arise and save us!" (2:27).
"But where are your gods that you made for yourself? Let them arise, if they can save you, in your time of trouble; for as many as your cities are your gods, O Judah" (2:28).
"Why do you contend with me? You have all transgressed against me," declares il SIGNORE (2:29).
"In vain have I struck your children; they took no correction. Your own sword devoured your prophets like a ravening lion" (2:30).
"And you, O generation, behold the word of il SIGNORE. Have I been a wilderness to Israel, or a land of thick darkness? Why then do my people say, 'We are free, we will come no more to you'?" (2:31).
"Can a virgin forget her ornaments, or a bride her attire? Yet my people have forgotten me days without number" (2:32).
"How well you direct your course to seek love! So that even to wicked women you have taught your ways" (2:33).
"Also on your skirts is found the lifeblood of the guiltless poor; you did not find them breaking in. Yet in spite of all these things" (2:34),
you say, "I am innocent; surely his anger has turned from me." Behold, I will bring you to judgment for saying, "I have not sinned" (2:35).
"How much you go about, changing your way! You shall be put to shame by Egypt as you were put to shame by Assyria" (2:36).
From there also you will come away with your hands on your head, for il SIGNORE has rejected those in whom you trust, and you will not prosper by them (2:37).

stories.title: 💧 Geremia 3
summaryBullets: "If a man divorces his wife and she goes from him and becomes another man's wife, will he return to her? Would not that land be greatly polluted? You have played the whore with many lovers; and would you return to me?" declares il SIGNORE (3:1).

«Alza gli occhi verso le alture e guarda. Dov’è che non ti sei prostituita? Tu sedevi per le vie ad aspettare i passanti, come fa l’Arabo nel deserto, e hai contaminato il paese con le tue prostituzioni e con le tue malvagità. (3:2).
Therefore the showers have been withheld, and the spring rain has not come; yet you have the forehead of a whore; you refuse to be ashamed (3:3).
"Have you not just now called to me, 'My father, you are the friend of my youth'" (3:4)?
"Will he be angry forever, will he be indignant to the end?" Behold, you have spoken, but you have done all the evil that you could (3:5).
Il Signore mi disse al tempo del re Giosia: «Hai visto ciò che l’infedele Israele ha fatto? È andata sopra ogni alto monte e sotto ogni albero verdeggiante, e là s’è prostituita. (3:6).
"And I thought, 'After she has done all this she will return to me,' but she did not return, and her treacherous sister Judah saw it" (3:7).

"She saw that for all the adulteries of that faithless one, Israel, I had sent her away with a decree of divorce. Yet her treacherous sister Judah did not fear, but she too went and played the whore" (3:8).
"Because she took her whoredom lightly, she polluted the land, committing adultery with stone and tree" (3:9).
"Yet for all this her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with her whole heart, but in pretense," declares il SIGNORE (3:10).
And il SIGNORE said to Jeremiah, "Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah" (3:11).

"Go, and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, 'Return, faithless Israel,' declares il SIGNORE. 'I will not look on you in anger, for I am merciful,' declares il SIGNORE; 'I will not be angry forever'" (3:12).

"Only acknowledge your guilt, that you rebelled against il SIGNORE your God and scattered your favors among foreigners under every green tree, and that you have not obeyed my voice," declares il SIGNORE (3:13).
"Return, O faithless children," declares il SIGNORE, "for I am your master; I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion" (3:14).
"And I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding" (3:15).

Quando sarete moltiplicati e avrete fruttato nel paese, allora», dice il Signore, «non si dirà più: “L’arca del patto del Signore!” Non vi si penserà più, non la si menzionerà più, non la si rimpiangerà più, non se ne farà un’altra. (3:16).
Allora Gerusalemme sarà chiamata il trono del Signore; tutte le nazioni si raduneranno a Gerusalemme nel nome del Signore e non cammineranno più secondo la caparbietà del loro cuore malvagio. (3:17).
In quei giorni la casa di Giuda camminerà con la casa d’Israele; verranno assieme dal paese del settentrione al paese che io diedi in eredità ai vostri padri. (3:18).

"I said, 'How I would set you among my sons, and give you a pleasant land, a heritage most beautiful of all nations.' And I thought you would call me 'My Father,' and would not turn from following me" (3:19).
"Surely, as a treacherous wife leaves her husband, so have you been treacherous to me, O house of Israel," declares il SIGNORE (3:20).
A voice is heard on the bare heights, the weeping and pleading of Israel's sons because they have perverted their way; they have forgotten il SIGNORE their God (3:21).
"Return, O faithless sons; I will heal your faithlessness." "Behold, we come to you, for you are il SIGNORE our God" (3:22).
"Truly the hills are a delusion, the orgies on the mountains. Truly in il SIGNORE our God is the salvation of Israel" (3:23).
"But the shameful thing has devoured all for which our fathers labored, from our youth—their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters" (3:24).

"Let us lie down in our shame, and let our dishonor cover us. For we have sinned against il SIGNORE our God, we and our fathers, from our youth even to this day, and we have not obeyed the voice of il SIGNORE our God" (3:25).

stories.title: 🧭 Geremia 4
summaryBullets: "If you return, O Israel," declares il SIGNORE, "to me you should return. If you remove your detestable things from my presence, and do not waver" (4:1),
"and if you swear, 'As il SIGNORE lives,' in truth, in justice, and in righteousness, then nations shall bless themselves in him, and in him shall they glory" (4:2).
For thus says il SIGNORE to the men of Judah and Jerusalem: "Break up your fallow ground, and sow not among thorns" (4:3).

"Circumcise yourselves to il SIGNORE; remove the foreskin of your hearts, O men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem; lest my wrath go forth like fire, and burn with none to quench it, because of the evil of your deeds" (4:4).
"Declare in Judah, and proclaim in Jerusalem, and say, 'Blow the trumpet through the land; cry aloud and say, "Assemble, and let us go into the fortified cities!"'" (4:5).
"Raise a standard toward Zion, flee for safety, stay not, for I bring disaster from the north, and great destruction" (4:6).

Un leone balza fuori dal folto bosco, un distruttore di nazioni si è messo in marcia, ha lasciato il suo luogo per ridurre il tuo paese in desolazione, al punto che le tue città saranno rovinate e prive di abitanti. (4:7).
For this put on sackcloth, lament and wail, for the fierce anger of il SIGNORE has not turned back from us (4:8).
«In quel giorno avverrà», dice il Signore, «che il cuore del re e il cuore dei capi verranno meno, i sacerdoti saranno attoniti, i profeti stupefatti». (4:9).
Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD, surely you have utterly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, 'It shall be well with you,' whereas the sword has reached their very life" (4:10).
In quel tempo si dirà a questo popolo e a Gerusalemme: «Un vento infuocato viene dalle alture del deserto verso la figlia del mio popolo, non per vagliare, non per nettare il grano; (4:11).
"a wind too full for this comes for me. Now it is I who speak in judgment upon them" (4:12).
"Behold, he comes up like clouds; his chariots like the whirlwind; his horses are swifter than eagles—woe to us, for we are ruined!" (4:13).
"O Jerusalem, wash the evil from your heart, that you may be saved. How long shall your wicked thoughts lodge within you?" (4:14).
For a voice declares from Dan and proclaims trouble from Mount Ephraim (4:15).
"Warn the nations that he is coming; announce to Jerusalem, 'Besiegers come from a distant land; they shout against the cities of Judah'" (4:16).
"Like keepers of a field are they against her all around, because she has rebelled against me," declares il SIGNORE (4:17).
"Your ways and your deeds have brought this upon you. This is your doom, and it is bitter; it has reached your very heart" (4:18).
"My anguish, my anguish! I writhe in pain! Oh the walls of my heart! My heart is beating wildly; I cannot keep silent, for I hear the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war" (4:19).
Crash follows crash; the whole land is laid waste. Suddenly my tents are laid waste, my curtains in a moment (4:20).
"How long must I see the standard and hear the sound of the trumpet?" (4:21).
"For my people are foolish; they know me not; they are stupid children; they have no understanding. They are 'wise'—in doing evil! But how to do good they know not" (4:22).
I looked at the earth, and behold, it was without form and void; and at the heavens, and they had no light (4:23).
I looked at the mountains, and behold, they were quaking, and all the hills moved to and fro (4:24).
Guardo, ed ecco, non c’è uomo; tutti gli uccelli del cielo sono volati via. (4:25).
I looked, and behold, the fruitful land was a desert, and all its cities were laid in ruins before il SIGNORE, before his fierce anger (4:26).
For thus says il SIGNORE, "The whole land shall be a desolation; yet I will not make a full end" (4:27).
For this the earth shall mourn, and the heavens above be dark; for I have spoken, I have purposed; I have not relented, nor will I turn back (4:28).
At the noise of horseman and archer every city takes to flight; they enter thickets, they climb among rocks. All the cities are forsaken, and no man dwells in them (4:29).

And you, O desolate one, what do you mean that you dress in scarlet, that you adorn yourself with ornaments of gold, that you enlarge your eyes with paint? In vain you beautify yourself; your lovers despise you; they seek your life (4:30).

For I heard a cry as of a woman in labor, anguish as of one giving birth to her first child, the cry of the daughter of Zion gasping for breath, stretching out her hands: "Woe is me! I am fainting before murderers" (4:31).

stories.title: 🔎 Geremia 5
summaryBullets: "Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, look and take note! Search her squares to see if you can find a man, one who does justice and seeks truth, that I may pardon her" (5:1).
Though they say, "As il SIGNORE lives," they swear falsely (5:2).

O LORD, do not your eyes look for truth? You have struck them down, but they felt no anguish; you have consumed them, but they refused to take correction. They have made their faces harder than rock; they have refused to repent (5:3).
Then I said, "These are only the poor; they have no sense; for they do not know the way of il SIGNORE, the justice of their God" (5:4).
"I will go to the great and will speak to them, for they know the way of il SIGNORE, the justice of their God." But they all alike had broken the yoke; they had burst the bonds (5:5).

Perciò il leone della foresta li uccide, il lupo del deserto li distrugge, il leopardo sta in agguato presso le loro città; chiunque ne uscirà sarà sbranato, perché le loro trasgressioni sono numerose, le loro infedeltà sono aumentate. (5:6).

«Perché ti dovrei perdonare? I tuoi figli mi hanno abbandonato, giurano per degli dèi che non esistono. Io li ho saziati ed essi si danno all’adulterio, si affollano nella casa della prostituta. (5:7).
They were well-fed, lusty stallions, each neighing for his neighbor's wife (5:8).
"Shall I not punish them for these things?" declares il SIGNORE; "and shall I not avenge myself on a nation such as this?" (5:9).
"Go up through her vine rows and destroy, but make not a full end; strip away her branches, for they are not il SIGNORE's" (5:10).
Infatti la casa d’Israele e la casa di Giuda mi hanno tradito», dice il Signore. (5:11).
They have spoken falsely of il SIGNORE and have said, "He will do nothing; no disaster will come upon us, nor shall we see sword or famine" (5:12).
The prophets will become wind; the word is not in them. Thus shall it be done to them! (5:13).
Therefore thus says il SIGNORE, the God of hosts: "Because you have spoken this word, behold, I am making my words in your mouth a fire, and this people wood, and the fire shall consume them" (5:14).

"Behold, I am bringing against you a nation from afar, O house of Israel," declares il SIGNORE. "It is an enduring nation; it is an ancient nation, a nation whose language you do not know, nor can you understand what they say" (5:15).
Their quiver is like an open tomb; they are all mighty warriors (5:16).

They shall eat up your harvest and your food; they shall eat up your sons and your daughters; they shall eat up your flocks and your herds; they shall eat up your vines and your fig trees; your fortified cities in which you trust they shall beat down with the sword (5:17).
"But even in those days," declares il SIGNORE, "I will not make a full end of you" (5:18).

Quando direte: “Perché il Signore, il nostro Dio, ci ha fatto tutto questo?”, tu risponderai loro: “Come voi mi avete abbandonato e avete servito dèi stranieri nel vostro paese, così servirete gli stranieri in un paese che non è vostro”. (5:19).
"Declare this in the house of Jacob; proclaim it in Judah" (5:20):
"Hear this, O foolish and senseless people, who have eyes, but see not, who have ears, but hear not" (5:21).

"Do you not fear me?" declares il SIGNORE. "Do you not tremble before me? I placed the sand as the boundary for the sea, a perpetual barrier that it cannot pass; though the waves toss, they cannot prevail; though they roar, they cannot pass over it" (5:22).
"But this people has a stubborn and rebellious heart; they have turned aside and gone away" (5:23).

Non dicono in cuor loro: ‘Temiamo il Signore, il nostro Dio, che dà la pioggia a suo tempo: la pioggia della prima e dell’ultima stagione, che ci mantiene le settimane fissate per la mietitura’. (5:24).
Your iniquities have turned these away, and your sins have kept good from you (5:25).
For wicked men are found among my people; they lurk like fowlers lying in wait. They set a trap; they catch men (5:26).
Like a cage full of birds, their houses are full of deceit; therefore they have become great and rich (5:27).
Ingrassano, hanno il volto lucido, oltrepassano ogni limite di male. Non difendono la causa, la causa dell’orfano, eppure prosperano; non fanno giustizia nei processi dei poveri. (5:28).
"Shall I not punish them for these things?" declares il SIGNORE, "and shall I not avenge myself on a nation such as this?" (5:29).
An appalling and horrible thing has happened in the land (5:30):
the prophets prophesy falsely, and il sacerdotes rule at their direction; my people love to have it so, but what will you do when the end comes? (5:31).

stories.title: 📣 Geremia 6
summaryBullets: «Figli di Beniamino, cercate un rifugio lontano da Gerusalemme; suonate la tromba in Tecoa; innalzate un segnale su Bet-Cherem, perché dal settentrione avanza una calamità, una grande rovina. (6:1).
The lovely and delicate one, the daughter of Zion, I will destroy (6:2).
Shepherds with their flocks shall come against her; they shall pitch their tents around her; they shall pasture, each in his place (6:3).
Preparate l’attacco contro di lei; alzatevi, saliamo in pieno mezzogiorno! Guai a noi, perché il giorno declina e le ombre della sera si allungano! (6:4).
"Arise, and let us attack by night and destroy her palaces!" (6:5).
For thus says il SIGNORE of hosts: "Cut down her trees; cast up a siege mound against Jerusalem. This is the city that must be punished; there is nothing but oppression within her" (6:6).
As a well keeps its water fresh, so she keeps fresh her evil; violence and destruction are heard within her; sickness and wounds are ever before me (6:7).
"Be warned, O Jerusalem, lest I turn from you in disgust, lest I make you a desolation, an uninhabited land" (6:8).
Thus says il SIGNORE of hosts: "They shall glean thoroughly as a vine the remnant of Israel; like a grape gatherer pass your hand again over its branches" (6:9).

To whom shall I speak and give warning, that they may hear? Behold, their ears are uncircumcised, they cannot listen; behold, the word of il SIGNORE is to them an object of scorn; they take no pleasure in it (6:10).

Ma io sono pieno del furore del Signore; sono stanco di contenermi. Rivèrsalo sui bambini per la strada e sui giovani riuniti assieme; poiché il marito e la moglie, il vecchio e l’uomo carico d’anni saranno presi tutti insieme. (6:11).
Le loro case saranno passate ad altri, così pure i loro campi e le loro mogli, poiché io stenderò la mia mano sugli abitanti del paese», dice il Signore. (6:12).
«Infatti, dal più piccolo al più grande, sono tutti quanti avidi di guadagno; dal profeta al sacerdote, tutti praticano la menzogna. (6:13).
They have healed the wound of my people lightly, saying, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace (6:14).

Saranno confusi perché commettono delle abominazioni. Non si vergognano affatto, non sanno che cosa sia arrossire, perciò cadranno fra quelli che cadono; quando io li visiterò saranno abbattuti», dice il Signore. (6:15).

Thus says il SIGNORE: "Stand by the roads, and look, and ask for the ancient paths, where the good way is; and walk in it, and find rest for your souls. But they said, 'We will not walk in it'" (6:16).
Io ho messo delle sentinelle per voi: “State attenti al suono della tromba!” Ma quelli rispondono: “Non staremo attenti”. (6:17).
Therefore hear, O nations, and know, O congregation, what will happen to them (6:18).
Hear, O earth; behold, I am bringing disaster upon this people, the fruit of their devices, because they have not paid attention to my words; and as for my law, they have rejected it (6:19).
"What use to me is frankincense that comes from Sheba, or sweet cane from a distant land? Your olocaustos are not acceptable, nor your sacrifices pleasing to me" (6:20).
Therefore thus says il SIGNORE: "Behold, I will lay before this people stumbling blocks against which they shall stumble; fathers and sons together, neighbor and friend shall perish" (6:21).
Così parla il Signore: «Ecco un popolo viene dal paese di settentrione, una grande nazione si muove dalle estremità della terra. (6:22).

They lay hold on bow and javelin; they are cruel and have no mercy; the sound of them is like the roaring sea; they ride on horses, set in array as a man for battle, against you, O daughter of Zion! (6:23).
"We have heard the report of it; our hands fall helpless; anguish has taken hold of us, pain as of a woman in labor" (6:24).
"Go not out into the field, nor walk on the road, for the enemy has a sword; terror is on every side" (6:25).
O daughter of my people, put on sackcloth, and roll in ashes; make mourning as for an only son, most bitter lamentation, for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us (6:26).
"I have made you a tester of metals among my people, that you may know and test their ways" (6:27).
They are all stubbornly rebellious, going about with slanders; they are bronze and iron; they all act corruptly (6:28).
The bellows blow fiercely; the lead is consumed by the fire; in vain the refining goes on, for the wicked are not removed (6:29).
Rejected silver they are called, for il SIGNORE has rejected them (6:30).

stories.title: 🕍 Geremia 7
summaryBullets: Ecco la parola che fu rivolta a Geremia da parte del Signore: (7:1).
"Hear the word of il SIGNORE, all you men of Judah who enter these gates to worship il SIGNORE" (7:2).
Thus says il SIGNORE of hosts, the God of Israel: "Amend your ways and your deeds, and I will let you dwell in this place" (7:3).
"Do not trust in these deceptive words: 'This is the temple of il SIGNORE, the temple of il SIGNORE, the temple of il SIGNORE'" (7:4).
"For if you truly amend your ways and your deeds, if you truly execute justice one with another" (7:5),
"if you do not oppress the sojourner, the fatherless, or the widow, or shed innocent blood in this place, and if you do not go after other gods to your own harm" (7:6),
"then I will let you dwell in this place, in the land that I gave of old to your fathers forever" (7:7).
"Behold, you trust in deceptive words to no avail" (7:8).
"Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, make offerings to Baal, and go after other gods that you have not known" (7:9),
"and then come and stand before me in this house, which is called by my name, and say, 'We are delivered!'—only to go on doing all these abominations?" (7:10).
"Has this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, I myself have seen it," declares il SIGNORE (7:11).
"Go now to my place that was in Shiloh, where I made my name dwell at first, and see what I did to it because of the evil of my people Israel" (7:12).
"And now, because you have done all these things," declares il SIGNORE, "and when I spoke to you persistently you did not listen, and when I called you, you did not answer" (7:13),
io tratterò questa casa, sulla quale è invocato il mio nome e nella quale riponete la vostra fiducia, e il luogo che ho dato a voi e ai vostri padri, come ho trattato Silo: (7:14).
"And I will cast you out of my sight, as I cast out all your kinsmen, all the offspring of Ephraim" (7:15).
"As for you, do not pray for this people, or lift up a cry or prayer for them, and do not intercede with me, for I will not hear you" (7:16).
Non vedi ciò che fanno nelle città di Giuda e nelle vie di Gerusalemme? (7:17).
I figli raccolgono legna, i padri accendono il fuoco, le donne impastano la farina per fare delle focacce alla regina del cielo e per fare libazioni ad altri dèi, per offendermi. (7:18).
"Is it I whom they provoke?" declares il SIGNORE. "Is it not themselves, to their own shame?" (7:19).

Perciò così parla il Signore, Dio: «Ecco, la mia ira, il mio furore, si riversa su questo luogo, sugli uomini e sulle bestie, sugli alberi della campagna e sui frutti della terra; essa consumerà ogni cosa e non si estinguerà». (7:20).
Thus says il SIGNORE of hosts, the God of Israel: "Add your olocaustos to your sacrifices, and eat the flesh" (7:21).
"For in the day that I brought them out of il paese d’Egitto, I did not speak to your fathers or command them concerning olocaustos and sacrifices" (7:22).
"But this command I gave them: 'Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people. And walk in all the way that I command you, that it may be well with you'" (7:23).
But they did not obey or incline their ear, but walked in their own counsels and the stubbornness of their evil hearts, and went backward and not forward (7:24).
From the day that your fathers came out of il paese d’Egitto to this day, I have persistently sent all my servants the prophets to them, day after day (7:25).
Yet they did not listen to me or incline their ear, but stiffened their neck. They did worse than their fathers (7:26).
Di’ loro tutte queste cose, ma essi non ti ascolteranno; chiamali, ma essi non ti risponderanno. (7:27).
"And you shall say to them, 'This is the nation that did not obey the voice of il SIGNORE their God, and did not accept discipline. Truth has perished; it is cut off from their lips'" (7:28).
"Cut off your hair and cast it away; raise a lamentation on the bare heights, for il SIGNORE has rejected and forsaken the generation of his wrath" (7:29).
"For i figli di Judah have done evil in my sight," declares il SIGNORE. "They have set their detestable things in the house that is called by my name, to defile it" (7:30).

Hanno costruito gli alti luoghi di Tofet nella valle del figlio di Innom, per bruciarvi nel fuoco i loro figli e le loro figlie, cosa che io non avevo comandata e che non mi era venuta in mente. (7:31).

Perciò, ecco, i giorni vengono», dice il Signore, «che non si dirà più Tofet né la valle del figlio di Innom, ma la valle del massacro, e, per mancanza di spazio, si seppelliranno i morti a Tofet. (7:32).
I cadaveri di questo popolo serviranno di pasto agli uccelli del cielo e alle bestie della terra, e non ci sarà nessuno che li scacci. (7:33).
Farò cessare nelle città di Giuda e per le strade di Gerusalemme il grido di gioia e il grido di esultanza, il canto dello sposo e il canto della sposa, perché il paese sarà una desolazione. (7:34).

translationNotes.note: Non un luogo di giustizia, ma un rifugio per malfattori violenti (7:11).

stories.title: 🕍 Geremia 8
summaryBullets: «In quel tempo», dice il Signore, «si toglieranno dai loro sepolcri le ossa dei re di Giuda, le ossa dei suoi prìncipi, le ossa dei sacerdoti, le ossa dei profeti, le ossa degli abitanti di Gerusalemme, (8:1).

e le si esporrà davanti al sole, davanti alla luna e davanti a tutto l’esercito del cielo, che essi hanno amato, hanno servito, hanno seguito, hanno consultato e davanti a cui si sono prostrati; non si raccoglieranno, non si seppelliranno, ma saranno come letame sulla faccia della terra. (8:2).
"Death shall be preferred to life by all the remnant that remains of this evil family in all the places where I have driven them," declares il SIGNORE of hosts (8:3).
"You shall say to them, Thus says il SIGNORE: When men fall, do they not rise again? If one turns away, does he not return?" (8:4).
"Why then has this people turned away in perpetual backsliding? They hold fast to deceit; they refuse to return" (8:5).

I have paid attention and listened, but they have not spoken rightly; no man relents of his evil, saying, "What have I done?" Everyone turns to his own course, like a horse plunging headlong into battle (8:6).
Anche la cicogna conosce nel cielo le sue stagioni; la tortora, la rondine e la gru osservano il tempo quando debbono venire, ma il mio popolo non conosce quel che il Signore ha ordinato. (8:7).
Voi come potete dire: ‘Noi siamo saggi e la legge del Signore è con noi!’? Sì, certo, ma la penna bugiarda degli scribi ha mentito. (8:8).
I saggi saranno confusi, saranno costernati, saranno presi. Ecco, hanno rigettato la parola del Signore; quale saggezza possono avere? (8:9).

Perciò io darò le loro mogli ad altri, i loro campi a dei nuovi possessori; poiché, dal più piccolo al più grande, sono tutti avidi di guadagno; dal profeta al sacerdote, tutti praticano la menzogna. (8:10).
They have healed the wound of the daughter of my people lightly, saying, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace (8:11).

Essi saranno confusi perché commettono delle abominazioni. Non si vergognano affatto, non sanno che cosa sia arrossire, perciò cadranno fra quelli che cadono; quando io li visiterò saranno abbattuti”, dice il Signore. (8:12).
"When I would gather them," declares il SIGNORE, "there are no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree; even the leaves are withered, and what I gave them has passed away from them" (8:13).

"Why do we sit still? Gather together; let us go into the fortified cities and perish there, for il SIGNORE our God has doomed us to perish and has given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against il SIGNORE" (8:14).
We looked for peace, but no good came; for a time of healing, but behold, terror (8:15).

Si ode da Dan lo sbuffare dei suoi cavalli; al rumore del nitrito dei suoi destrieri trema tutto il paese; poiché vengono, divorano il paese e tutto ciò che contiene, la città e i suoi abitanti. (8:16).
"For behold, I am sending among you serpents, adders that cannot be charmed, and they shall bite you," declares il SIGNORE (8:17).
My joy is gone; grief is upon me; my heart is sick within me (8:18).

Ecco il grido d’angoscia della figlia del mio popolo da terra lontana: «Il Signore non è più in Sion? Il suo re non è più in mezzo a lei?» «Perché hanno provocato la mia ira con le loro immagini scolpite e con vanità straniere?» (8:19).
"The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved" (8:20).
Per la piaga della figlia del mio popolo io sono tutto affranto; sono in lutto, sono in preda alla costernazione. (8:21).
Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there? Why then has the health of the daughter of my people not been restored? (8:22).

stories.title: 💧 Geremia 9
summaryBullets: Oh, fosse la mia testa piena d’acqua e i miei occhi una fonte di lacrime! Io piangerei giorno e notte gli uccisi della figlia del mio popolo! (9:1).
Oh that I had in the desert a travelers' lodging place, that I might leave my people and go away from them! For they are all adulterers, a company of treacherous men (9:2).
They bend their tongue like a bow; falsehood and not truth has grown strong in the land; for they proceed from evil to evil, and they do not know me, declares il SIGNORE (9:3).
Let everyone beware of his neighbor, and put no trust in any brother, for every brother is a deceiver, and every neighbor goes about as a slanderer (9:4).
Everyone deceives his neighbor, and no one speaks the truth; they have taught their tongue to speak lies; they weary themselves committing iniquity (9:5).
"You dwell in the midst of deceit; in deceit they refuse to know me," declares il SIGNORE (9:6).
Therefore thus says il SIGNORE of hosts: "Behold, I will refine them and test them, for what else can I do, because of my people?" (9:7).
Their tongue is a deadly arrow; it speaks deceitfully; with his mouth each speaks peace to his neighbor, but in his heart he plans an ambush (9:8).
"Shall I not punish them for these things?" declares il SIGNORE, "and shall I not avenge myself on a nation such as this?" (9:9).

Io voglio prorompere in pianto e in gemito per i monti; voglio spandere un lamento per i pascoli del deserto, perché sono bruciati, al punto che nessuno più vi passa, non vi si ode più muggito di mandrie; gli uccelli del cielo e le bestie sono fuggite, sono scomparse. (9:10).
"I will make Jerusalem a heap of ruins, a lair of jackals, and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant" (9:11).

Who is the man so wise that he can understand this? To whom has the mouth of il SIGNORE spoken, that he may declare it? Why is the land ruined and laid waste like a wilderness, so that no one passes through? (9:12).
And il SIGNORE says: "Because they have forsaken my law that I set before them, and have not obeyed my voice or walked in accord with it" (9:13),
"but have stubbornly followed their own hearts and have gone after the Baals, as their fathers taught them" (9:14).
Therefore thus says il SIGNORE of hosts, the God of Israel: "Behold, I will feed this people with bitter food, and give them poisonous water to drink" (9:15).
"I will scatter them among the nations whom neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send the sword after them, until I have consumed them" (9:16).
Così parla il Signore degli eserciti: «Pensate a chiamare delle piagnone, e che esse vengano! Invitate le più accorte, e che esse vengano (9:17).
"Let them make haste and raise a wailing over us, that our eyes may run down with tears and our eyelids flow with water" (9:18).
For a sound of wailing is heard from Zion: "How we are ruined! We are utterly shamed, because we have left the land, because they have cast down our dwellings" (9:19).

Poiché la morte è salita alle nostre finestre, è entrata nei nostri palazzi per far sparire i bambini dalle strade e i giovani dalle piazze. (9:21).

stories.title: 💧 Geremia 10
summaryBullets: Hear the word that il SIGNORE speaks to you, O house of Israel (10:1).
Così parla il Signore: «Non imparate a camminare nella via delle nazioni e non abbiate paura dei segni del cielo, perché sono le nazioni quelle che ne hanno paura. (10:2).
Infatti i costumi dei popoli sono vanità; poiché si taglia un albero nella foresta e le mani dell’operaio lo lavorano con l’ascia, (10:3).
They decorate it with silver and gold; they fasten it with hammer and nails so that it cannot move (10:4).

Their idols are like scarecrows in a cucumber field, and they cannot speak; they have to be carried, for they cannot walk. Do not be afraid of them, for they cannot do evil, neither is it in them to do good (10:5).
There is none like you, O LORD; you are great, and your name is great in might (10:6).
Chi non ti temerebbe, re delle nazioni? Poiché questo ti è dovuto; poiché fra tutti i saggi delle nazioni e in tutti i loro regni non c’è nessuno pari a te. (10:7).
They are both stupid and foolish; the instruction of idols is but wood! (10:8).
argento battuto in lastre portato da Tarsis, oro venuto da Ufaz, opera di scultore e di mano d’orefice; sono vestiti di porpora e di scarlatto, sono tutti lavoro di abili artefici. (10:9).
Ma il Signore è il vero Dio, egli è il Dio vivente e il re eterno; per la sua ira trema la terra e le nazioni non possono resistere davanti al suo sdegno. (10:10).
«Così direte loro: “Gli dèi che non hanno fatto i cieli e la terra scompariranno dalla terra e da sotto il cielo”». (10:11).
It is he who made the earth by his power, who established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding stretched out the heavens (10:12).
Quando fa udire la sua voce, c’è un rumore di acque nel cielo; egli fa salire i vapori dalle estremità della terra, fa guizzare i lampi per la pioggia e sprigiona il vento dai suoi serbatoi. (10:13).
Every man is stupid and without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols, for his images are false, and there is no breath in them (10:14).
They are worthless, a work of delusion; at the time of their punishment they shall perish (10:15).
Not like these is he who is the portion of Jacob, for he is the one who formed all things, and Israel is la tribù di his inheritance; il SIGNORE of hosts is his name (10:16).
Gather up your bundle from the ground, O you who dwell under siege! (10:17).
For thus says il SIGNORE: "Behold, I am slinging out the inhabitants of the land at this time, and I will bring distress on them, that they may feel it" (10:18).
Woe is me because of my hurt! My wound is grievous. But I said, "Truly this is an affliction, and I must bear it" (10:19).
My tent is destroyed, and all my cords are broken; my children have gone from me, and they are not; there is no one to spread my tent again and to set up my curtains (10:20).
For the shepherds are stupid and do not inquire of il SIGNORE; therefore they have not prospered, and all their flock is scattered (10:21).
Così parla il Signore: «Non imparate a camminare nella via delle nazioni e non abbiate paura dei segni del cielo, perché sono le nazioni quelle che ne hanno paura. (10:22).
I know, O LORD, that the way of man is not in himself, that it is not in man who walks to direct his steps (10:23).
Correct me, O LORD, but in justice; not in your anger, lest you bring me to nothing (10:24).

Pour out your wrath on the nations that know you not, and on the peoples that call not on your name, for they have devoured Jacob; they have devoured him and consumed him, and have laid waste his habitation (10:25).

stories.title: 📜 Geremia 11
summaryBullets: The word that came to Jeremiah from il SIGNORE (11:1):
«Ascoltate le parole di questo patto e parlate agli uomini di Giuda e agli abitanti di Gerusalemme! (11:2).
"You shall say to them, Thus says il SIGNORE, the God of Israel: Cursed be the man who does not hear the words of this covenant" (11:3),

"that I commanded your fathers when I brought them out of il paese d’Egitto, from the iron furnace, saying, Listen to my voice, and do all that I command you. So shall you be my people, and I will be your God" (11:4),
"that I may confirm the oath that I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as at this day." Then I answered, "Amen, LORD" (11:5).
Il Signore mi disse: «Proclama tutte queste parole nelle città di Giuda e per le strade di Gerusalemme, dicendo: “Ascoltate le parole di questo patto e mettetele in pratica! (11:6).
For I solemnly warned your fathers when I brought them up out of il paese d’Egitto, warning them persistently, even to this day, saying, Obey my voice (11:7).

Yet they did not obey or incline their ear, but everyone walked in the stubbornness of his evil heart. Therefore I brought upon them all the words of this covenant, which I commanded them to do, but they did not (11:8).
Poi il Signore mi disse: «Esiste una congiura tra gli uomini di Giuda e fra gli abitanti di Gerusalemme. (11:9).

Sono tornati alle iniquità dei loro padri antichi, i quali rifiutarono di ascoltare le mie parole; sono andati anch’essi dietro ad altri dèi, per servirli. La casa d’Israele e la casa di Giuda hanno rotto il patto che io avevo fatto con i loro padri. (11:10).
Therefore, thus says il SIGNORE, "Behold, I am bringing disaster upon them that they cannot escape. Though they cry to me, I will not listen to them" (11:11).
Allora le città di Giuda e gli abitanti di Gerusalemme andranno a gridare agli dèi a cui offrono profumi; ma essi non li salveranno nel tempo della calamità! (11:12).
For your gods have become as many as your cities, O Judah, and as many as the streets of Jerusalem are the altars you have set up to shame, altars to make offerings to Baal (11:13).
"Therefore do not pray for this people, or lift up a cry or prayer on their behalf, for I will not listen when they call to me in the time of their trouble" (11:14).
"What right has my beloved in my house, when she has done many vile deeds? Can even sacrificial flesh avert your doom? Can you then exult?" (11:15).
The LORD once called you "a green olive tree, beautiful with good fruit." But with the roar of a great tempest he will set fire to it, and its branches will be consumed (11:16).

Il Signore degli eserciti che ti aveva piantato pronuncia del male contro di te, a causa della malvagità commessa a loro danno dalla casa d’Israele e dalla casa di Giuda, quando hanno provocato la mia ira offrendo profumi a Baal. (11:17).
The LORD made it known to me and I knew; then you showed me their deeds (11:18).

Io ero come un docile agnello che si conduce al macello; io non sapevo che tramavano macchinazioni contro di me, dicendo: «Distruggiamo l’albero con il suo frutto, sterminiamolo dalla terra dei viventi, affinché il suo nome non sia più ricordato». (11:19).
But, O LORD of hosts, who judges righteously, who tests the heart and the mind, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you have I committed my cause (11:20).
Therefore thus says il SIGNORE concerning the men of Anathoth, who seek your life, and say, "Do not prophesy in the name of il SIGNORE, or you will die by our hand" (11:21)—
therefore thus says il SIGNORE of hosts: "Behold, I will punish them. The young men shall die by the sword; their sons and their daughters shall die by famine" (11:22),
"and none of them shall be left. For I will bring disaster upon the men of Anathoth, the year of their punishment" (11:23).

stories.title: 📜 Geremia 12
summaryBullets: "Righteous are you, O LORD, when I complain to you; yet I would plead my case before you. Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why do all who are treacherous thrive?" (12:1).
You plant them, and they take root; they grow and produce fruit; you are near in their mouth and far from their heart (12:2).
Signore, tu mi conosci, tu mi vedi, tu provi quale sia il mio cuore verso di te. Trascinali al macello come pecore, preparali per il giorno del massacro! (12:3).

Fino a quando sarà afflitto il paese e si seccherà l’erba di tutta la campagna? Per la malvagità degli abitanti, le bestie e gli uccelli sono sterminati. Poiché quelli dicono: «Egli non vedrà la nostra fine». (12:4).
«Se correndo con dei pedoni, questi ti stancano, come potrai gareggiare con i cavalli? Se non ti senti al sicuro che in terra di pace, come farai quando il Giordano sarà in piena? (12:5).
For even your brothers and the house of your father, even they have dealt treacherously with you; they are in full cry after you; do not believe them, though they speak friendly words to you (12:6).
"I have forsaken my house; I have abandoned my heritage; I have given the beloved of my soul into the hands of her enemies" (12:7).
My heritage has become to me like a lion in the forest; she has lifted up her voice against me; therefore I hate her (12:8).
Is my heritage to me like a hyena's lair? Are the birds of prey against her all around? Go, assemble all the wild beasts; bring them to devour (12:9).
Many shepherds have destroyed my vineyard; they have trampled down my portion; they have made my pleasant portion a desolate wilderness (12:10).
They have made it a desolation; desolate, it mourns to me. The whole land is made desolate, but no man lays it to heart (12:11).
Su tutte le alture del deserto giungono devastatori, perché la spada del Signore divora il paese da un’estremità all’altra; non c’è pace per nessuno. (12:12).
Hanno seminato grano e raccolgono spine; si sono affannati senza alcun profitto. Vergognatevi di ciò che raccogliete a causa dell’ira ardente del Signore!» (12:13).

Thus says il SIGNORE concerning all my evil neighbors who touch the heritage that I have given my people Israel to inherit: "Behold, I will pluck them up from their land, and I will pluck up the house of Judah from among them" (12:14).
And after I have plucked them up, I will again have compassion on them, and I will bring them again each to his heritage and each to his land (12:15).

Se imparano diligentemente le vie del mio popolo e giurano per il mio nome, dicendo: “Il Signore vive”, come hanno insegnato al mio popolo a giurare per Baal, saranno saldamente stabiliti in mezzo al mio popolo. (12:16).
But if any nation will not listen, then I will utterly pluck it up and destroy it, declares il SIGNORE (12:17).

stories.title: 📜 Geremia 13
summaryBullets: Thus said il SIGNORE to me, "Go and buy a linen loincloth and put it around your waist, and do not dip it in water" (13:1).
So I bought a loincloth according to the word of il SIGNORE, and put it around my waist (13:2).
And the word of il SIGNORE came to me a second time, saying (13:3),
«Prendi la cintura che hai comprata e che hai attorno ai fianchi; va’ verso l’Eufrate e nascondila laggiù, nella fessura di una roccia». (13:4).
So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, as il SIGNORE commanded me (13:5).
Dopo molti giorni il Signore mi disse: «Àlzati, va’ verso l’Eufrate e togli di là la cintura che io ti avevo comandato di nascondervi». (13:6).
Io andai verso l’Eufrate, scavai e tolsi la cintura dal luogo dove l’avevo nascosta. Ecco, la cintura era marcita, non era più buona a nulla. (13:7).
Then the word of il SIGNORE came to me (13:8):
"Thus says il SIGNORE: Even so will I spoil the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem" (13:9).

"This evil people, who refuse to hear my words, who stubbornly follow their own heart and have gone after other gods to serve them and worship them, shall be like this loincloth, which is good for nothing" (13:10).

Infatti, come la cintura aderisce ai fianchi dell’uomo, così io avevo strettamente unita a me tutta la casa d’Israele e tutta la casa di Giuda”, dice il Signore, “perché fossero mio popolo, mia fama, mia lode, mia gloria; ma essi non hanno voluto dare ascolto”. (13:11).
«Tu dirai loro questa parola: “Così parla il Signore, Dio d’Israele: ‘Ogni otre sarà riempito di vino’”. E quando essi ti diranno: “Non lo sappiamo noi che ogni otre si riempie di vino?”, (13:12).

"Then you shall say to them, 'Thus says il SIGNORE: Behold, I will fill with drunkenness all the inhabitants of this land: the kings who sit on David's throne, il sacerdotes, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem'" (13:13).
"And I will dash them one against another, fathers and sons together," declares il SIGNORE. "I will not pity or spare or have compassion, that I should not destroy them" (13:14).
Hear and give ear; be not proud, for il SIGNORE has spoken (13:15).

Give glory to il SIGNORE your God before he brings darkness, before your feet stumble on the twilight mountains, and while you look for light he turns it into gloom and makes it deep darkness (13:16).
But if you will not listen, my soul will weep in secret for your pride; my eyes will weep bitterly and run down with tears, because il SIGNORE's flock has been taken captive (13:17).
Di’ al re e alla regina: «Sedetevi per terra! perché la vostra gloriosa corona vi cade dalla testa». (13:18).
Così mi ha detto il Signore: «Va’, còmprati una cintura di lino, mettitela attorno ai fianchi, ma non la porre nell’acqua». (13:19).
"Lift up your eyes and see those who come from the north. Where is the flock that was given you, your beautiful flock?" (13:20).
What will you say when they set as head over you those whom you yourself have taught to be friends to you? Will not pangs take hold of you like those of a woman in labor? (13:21).
And if you say in your heart, "Why have these things come upon me?" it is for the greatness of your iniquity that your skirts are lifted up and you suffer violence (13:22).
Can the Ethiopian change his skin or the leopard his spots? Then also you can do good who are accustomed to do evil (13:23).
"I will scatter you like chaff driven by the wind from the desert" (13:24).
"This is your lot, the portion I have measured out to you," declares il SIGNORE, "because you have forgotten me and trusted in lies" (13:25).
"I myself will lift up your skirts over your face, and your shame will be seen" (13:26).
I have seen your abominations, your adulteries and neighings, your lewd whorings, on the hills in the field. Woe to you, O Jerusalem! How long will it be before you are made clean? (13:27).

stories.title: 🌵 Geremia 14
summaryBullets: The word of il SIGNORE that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought (14:1):
"Judah mourns, and her gates languish; her people lament on the ground, and the cry of Jerusalem goes up" (14:2).
Her nobles send their servants for water; they come to the cisterns but find no water. They return with their vessels empty; they are ashamed and confounded and cover their heads (14:3).
Il suolo è costernato perché non c’è stata pioggia nel paese; i lavoratori sono pieni di confusione e si coprono il capo. (14:4).
Even the doe in the field forsakes her newborn fawn because there is no grass (14:5).
The wild donkeys stand on the bare heights; they pant for air like jackals; their eyes fail because there is no vegetation (14:6).
"Though our iniquities testify against us, act, O LORD, for your name's sake; for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against you" (14:7).
O you hope of Israel, its savior in time of trouble, why should you be like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who turns aside to tarry for a night? (14:8).
Why should you be like a man confused, like a mighty warrior who cannot save? Yet you, O LORD, are in the midst of us, and we are called by your name; do not leave us (14:9).

Thus says il SIGNORE concerning this people: "They have loved to wander thus; they have not restrained their feet; therefore il SIGNORE does not accept them; now he will remember their iniquity and punish their sins" (14:10).
Il Signore mi disse: «Non pregare per il bene di questo popolo. (14:11).

"Though they fast, I will not hear their cry, and though they offer olocausto and offerta di cereali, I will not accept them. But I will consume them by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence" (14:12).
Then I said: "Ah, Lord GOD, behold, the prophets say to them, 'You shall not see the sword, nor shall you have famine, but I will give you assured peace in this place'" (14:13).

Il Signore mi disse: «Quei profeti profetizzano menzogne nel mio nome; io non li ho mandati, non ho dato loro nessun ordine e non ho parlato loro. Le profezie che vi fanno sono visioni menzognere, divinazione, vanità, imposture del proprio cuore. (14:14).

Therefore thus says il SIGNORE concerning the prophets who prophesy in my name although I did not send them, and who say, "Sword and famine shall not come upon this land": By sword and famine those prophets shall be consumed (14:15).

e quelli ai quali essi profetizzano saranno gettati per le vie di Gerusalemme morti di fame e di spada, essi, le loro mogli, i loro figli e le loro figlie, né vi sarà chi dia loro sepoltura; riverserò su di loro la loro malvagità. (14:16).

Di’ loro dunque questa parola: “I miei occhi si sciolgano in lacrime giorno e notte, senza posa, poiché la vergine figlia del mio popolo è stata stroncata in modo straziante, ha ricevuto un colpo tremendo. (14:17).

If I go out into the field, behold, those pierced by the sword! And if I enter the city, behold, the diseases of famine! For both prophet and priest ply their trade through the land and have no knowledge (14:18).

"Have you utterly rejected Judah? Does your soul loathe Zion? Why have you struck us down so that there is no healing for us? We looked for peace, but no good came; for a time of healing, but behold, terror" (14:19).
We acknowledge our wickedness, O LORD, and the iniquity of our fathers, for we have sinned against you (14:20).
Do not spurn us, for your name's sake; do not dishonor your glorious throne; remember and do not break your covenant with us (14:21).
Are there any among the false gods of the nations that can bring rain? Or can the heavens give showers? Are you not he, O LORD our God? We set our hope on you, for you do all these things (14:22).

stories.title: 🌵 Geremia 15
summaryBullets: Il Signore mi disse: «Anche se Mosè e Samuele si presentassero davanti a me, io non mi piegherei verso questo popolo; caccialo via dalla mia presenza, e che egli se ne vada! (15:1).

Se anche ti dicono: “Dove ce ne andremo?”, tu risponderai loro: “Così dice il Signore: ‘Alla morte, i destinati alla morte; alla spada, i destinati alla spada; alla fame, i destinati alla fame; alla schiavitù, i destinati alla schiavitù’”. (15:2).

Io», dice il Signore, «manderò contro di loro quattro specie di flagelli: la spada, per ucciderli; i cani, per trascinarli; gli uccelli del cielo e le bestie della terra, per divorarli e per distruggerli. (15:3).
"And I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth because of what Manasseh figlio di Hezekiah, king of Judah, did in Jerusalem" (15:4).
"Who will have pity on you, O Jerusalem, or who will grieve for you? Who will turn aside to ask about your welfare?" (15:5).
"You have rejected me," declares il SIGNORE; "you keep going backward. So I have stretched out my hand against you and destroyed you—I am weary of relenting" (15:6).
Io ti ventilerò con il ventilabro alle porte del paese, priverò di figli il mio popolo e lo farò perire, poiché non si convertì dalle sue vie. (15:7).

"I have made their widows more in number than the sand of the seas; I have brought against the mothers of young men a destroyer at noonday; I have made anguish and terror fall upon them suddenly" (15:8).

Colei che aveva partorito sette figli è languente, esala l’ultimo respiro; il suo sole tramonta mentre è giorno ancora; è coperta di vergogna, di confusione; il rimanente di loro io lo do in balìa della spada dei loro nemici», dice il Signore. (15:9).
Woe is me, my mother, that you bore me, a man of strife and contention to the whole land! I have not lent, nor have I borrowed, yet all of them curse me (15:10).
Il Signore dice: «Per certo, io ti riservo un avvenire felice; io farò in modo che il nemico ti rivolga suppliche nel tempo dell’avversità, nel tempo dell’angoscia. (15:11).
"Can one break iron, iron from the north, and bronze?" (15:12).
"Your wealth and your treasures I will give as spoil, without price, for all your sins, throughout all your territory" (15:13).
"I will make you serve your enemies in a land that you do not know, for in my anger a fire is kindled that shall burn forever" (15:14).
O LORD, you know; remember me and visit me, and take vengeance for me on my persecutors. In your forbearance take me not away; know that for your sake I bear reproach (15:15).
Your words were found, and I ate them, and your words became to me a joy and the delight of my heart, for I am called by your name, O LORD, God of hosts (15:16).
I did not sit in the company of revelers, nor did I rejoice; I sat alone, because your hand was upon me, for you had filled me with indignation (15:17).
Why is my pain unceasing, my wound incurable, refusing to be healed? Will you be to me like a deceitful brook, like waters that fail? (15:18).

Perciò così parla il Signore: «Se torni a me, io ti farò ritornare e rimarrai davanti a me; e se tu separi ciò che è prezioso da ciò che è vile, tu sarai come la mia bocca. Essi ritorneranno a te, ma tu non tornerai a loro. (15:19).

"And I will make you to this people a fortified wall of bronze; they will fight against you, but they shall not prevail over you, for I am with you to save you and deliver you," declares il SIGNORE (15:20).
«Ti libererò dalla mano dei malvagi, ti salverò dalla mano dei violenti». (15:21).

stories.title: 🚫 Geremia 16
summaryBullets: The word of il SIGNORE came to Jeremiah (16:1):
"You shall not take a wife, nor shall you have sons or daughters in this place" (16:2).
Infatti così parla il Signore riguardo ai figli e alle figlie che nascono in questo paese, alle madri che li partoriscono e ai padri che li generano in questo paese: (16:3).

«Essi moriranno consumati dalle malattie, non saranno rimpianti e non avranno sepoltura; serviranno di letame sulla faccia della terra; saranno consumati dalla spada e dalla fame, e i loro cadaveri saranno pasto per gli uccelli del cielo e per le bestie della terra». (16:4).
"Do not enter the house of mourning, or go to lament or grieve for them, for I have taken away my peace from this people, my steadfast love and mercy," declares il SIGNORE (16:5).
Both great and small shall die in this land. They shall not be buried, and no one shall lament for them or cut himself or make himself bald for them (16:6).
non si spezzerà per loro il pane del lutto per consolarli di un morto, non si offrirà loro da bere la coppa della consolazione per un padre o per una madre. (16:7).
Allo stesso modo non entrare in nessuna casa di convito per sederti con loro a mangiare e a bere». (16:8).

Infatti così parla il Signore degli eserciti, Dio d’Israele: «Ecco, io farò cessare in questo luogo, davanti ai vostri occhi, ai giorni vostri, il grido di gioia, il grido d’esultanza, il canto dello sposo e il canto della sposa». (16:9).

"And when you tell this people all these words, and they say to you, 'Why has il SIGNORE pronounced all this great evil against us? What is our iniquity? What is the sin that we have committed against il SIGNORE our God?'" (16:10),

"then you shall say to them: 'Because your fathers have forsaken me,' declares il SIGNORE, 'and have gone after other gods and have served and worshiped them, and have forsaken me and have not kept my law'" (16:11),
"and because you have done worse than your fathers, for behold, every one of you follows his stubborn, evil will, refusing to listen to me" (16:12).
"Therefore I will hurl you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you shall serve other gods day and night, for I will show you no favor" (16:13).
"Therefore, behold, the days are coming," declares il SIGNORE, "when it shall no longer be said, 'As il SIGNORE lives who brought up i figli d’Israele out of il paese d’Egitto'" (16:14),

"but 'As il SIGNORE lives who brought up i figli d’Israele out of the north country and out of all the countries where he had driven them.' For I will bring them back to their own land that I gave to their fathers" (16:15).

Ecco, io mando un gran numero di pescatori a pescarli», dice il Signore; «inoltre manderò un gran numero di cacciatori a dar loro la caccia sopra ogni monte, sopra ogni collina e nelle fessure delle rocce. (16:16).
For my eyes are on all their ways. They are not hidden from me, nor is their iniquity concealed from my eyes (16:17).

But first I will doubly repay their iniquity and their sin, because they have polluted my land with the carcasses of their detestable idols, and have filled my inheritance with their abominations (16:18).

Signore, mia forza, mia fortezza e mio rifugio nel giorno dell’avversità! A te verranno le nazioni dalle estremità della terra e diranno: «I nostri padri non hanno ereditato che menzogne, vanità e cose che non giovano a nulla. (16:19).
Can man make for himself gods? Such are not gods! (16:20).
"Therefore, behold, I will make them know, this once I will make them know my power and my might, and they shall know that my name is il SIGNORE" (16:21).

stories.title: 🚫 Geremia 17
summaryBullets: "The sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron; with a point of diamond it is engraved on the tablet of their heart and on the horns of their altars" (17:1),
"while their children remember their altars and their Asherim, beside every green tree and on the high hills" (17:2),
"on the mountains in the open country. Your wealth and all your treasures I will give for spoil as the price of your high places for sin throughout all your territory" (17:3).

You shall loosen your hand from your heritage that I gave to you, and I will make you serve your enemies in a land that you do not know, for in my anger a fire is kindled that shall burn forever (17:4).
Thus says il SIGNORE: "Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his strength, whose heart turns away from il SIGNORE" (17:5).
Egli è come una tamerice nel deserto: quando giunge il bene, egli non lo vede; abita in luoghi aridi, nel deserto, in terra salata, senza abitanti. (17:6).
"Blessed is the man who trusts in il SIGNORE, whose trust is il SIGNORE" (17:7).

He is like a tree planted by water, that sends out its roots by the stream, and does not fear when heat comes, for its leaves remain green, and is not anxious in the year of drought, for it does not cease to bear fruit (17:8).
The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick; who can understand it? (17:9).
"I il SIGNORE search the heart and test the mind, to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his deeds" (17:10).
Like the partridge that gathers a brood that she did not hatch, so is he who gets riches but not by justice; in the midst of his days they will leave him, and at his end he will be a fool (17:11).
A glorious throne set on high from the beginning is the place of our sanctuary (17:12).

Speranza d’Israele, o Signore, tutti quelli che ti abbandonano saranno confusi; quelli che si allontanano da te saranno iscritti sulla polvere, perché hanno abbandonato il Signore, la sorgente delle acque vive. (17:13).
Guariscimi, Signore, e sarò guarito; salvami, e sarò salvo, poiché tu sei la mia lode. (17:14).
Behold, they say to me, "Where is the word of il SIGNORE? Let it come!" (17:15).
I have not run away from being your shepherd, nor have I desired the day of sickness. You know what came out of my lips; it was before your face (17:16).
Be not a terror to me; you are my refuge in the day of disaster (17:17).

Let those be put to shame who persecute me, but let me not be put to shame; let them be dismayed, but let me not be dismayed; bring upon them the day of disaster; destroy them with double destruction! (17:18).
Thus said il SIGNORE to me: "Go and stand in the People's Gate, by which the kings of Judah enter and by which they go out, and in all the gates of Jerusalem" (17:19),
"and say: 'Hear the word of il SIGNORE, you kings of Judah, and all Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, who enter by these gates'" (17:20).
Thus says il SIGNORE: "Take care for the sake of your lives, and do not bear a burden on the Sabbath day or bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem" (17:21).
"And do not carry a burden out of your houses on the Sabbath or do any work, but keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your fathers" (17:22).
Yet they did not listen or incline their ear, but stiffened their neck, that they might not hear and might not receive instruction (17:23).
"But if you listen to me," declares il SIGNORE, "and bring in no burden by the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, but keep the Sabbath day holy and do no work on it" (17:24),

i re e i prìncipi che siedono sul trono di Davide entreranno per le porte di questa città su carri e su cavalli: entreranno essi, i loro prìncipi, gli uomini di Giuda, gli abitanti di Gerusalemme; e questa città sarà abitata per sempre. (17:25).

Dalle città di Giuda, dai luoghi circostanti di Gerusalemme, dal paese di Beniamino, dalla pianura, dal monte e dalla regione meridionale si verrà a portare olocausti, vittime, offerte, incenso e a offrire sacrifici di ringraziamento nella casa del Signore. (17:26).

"But if you do not listen to me, to keep the Sabbath day holy, and not to bear a burden and enter by the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem and shall not be quenched" (17:27).

stories.title: 🏺 Geremia 18
summaryBullets: The word that came to Jeremiah from il SIGNORE (18:1):
"Arise, and go down to the potter's house, and there I will let you hear my words" (18:2).
Allora io scesi in casa del vasaio, ed ecco, egli stava lavorando alla ruota. (18:3).
Il vaso che faceva si guastò, come succede all’argilla in mano del vasaio; da capo ne fece un altro come a lui parve bene di farlo. (18:4).
Then the word of il SIGNORE came to me (18:5):
"O house of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter has done?" declares il SIGNORE. "Behold, like the clay in the potter's hand, so are you in my hand, O house of Israel" (18:6).
If at any time I declare concerning a nation or a kingdom, that I will pluck up and break down and destroy it (18:7),
and if that nation, concerning which I have spoken, turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I intended to do to it (18:8).
And if at any time I declare concerning a nation or a kingdom that I will build and plant it (18:9),
and if it does evil in my sight, not listening to my voice, then I will relent of the good that I had intended to do to it (18:10).

«Ora parla agli uomini di Giuda e agli abitanti di Gerusalemme e di’: “Così parla il Signore: ‘Ecco, io preparo contro di voi del male e formo contro di voi un disegno. Si converta ora ciascuno di voi dalla sua malvagità, cambiate le vostre vie e le vostre azioni!’”. (18:11).
But they say, "That is in vain! We will follow our own plans, and will every one act according to the stubbornness of his evil heart" (18:12).
Therefore thus says il SIGNORE: "Ask among the nations, Who has heard the like of this? The virgin Israel has done a very horrible thing" (18:13).
Does the snow of Lebanon leave the crags of Sirion? Do the mountain waters run dry, the cold flowing streams? (18:14).
But my people have forgotten me; they make offerings to false gods; they made them stumble in their ways, in the ancient roads, and to walk into side roads, not the highway (18:15),
making their land a horror, a thing to be hissed at forever. Everyone who passes by it is horrified and shakes his head (18:16).
Like the east wind I will scatter them before the enemy. I will show them my back, not my face, in the day of their calamity (18:17).

Essi hanno detto: «Venite, tramiamo insidie contro Geremia; poiché la legge non verrà meno per mancanza di sacerdoti, né il consiglio per mancanza di saggi, né la parola per mancanza di profeti. Venite, attacchiamolo con la lingua e non diamo retta a nessuna delle sue parole». (18:18).
Hear me, O LORD, and listen to the voice of my adversaries (18:19).
Should good be repaid with evil? Yet they have dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before you to speak good for them, to turn away your wrath from them (18:20).

Perciò abbandona i loro figli alla fame e dalli in balìa della spada; le loro mogli siano private di figli e rimangano vedove, i loro mariti siano feriti a morte; i loro giovani siano colpiti dalla spada in battaglia. (18:21).
May a cry be heard from their houses, when you bring the plunderer suddenly upon them! For they have dug a pit to take me and laid snares for my feet (18:22).

Yet you, O LORD, know all their plotting to kill me. Do not forgive their iniquity, nor blot out their sin from your sight. Let them be overthrown before you; deal with them in the time of your anger (18:23).

stories.title: 🏺 Geremia 19
summaryBullets: Così ha detto il Signore: «Va’, compra una brocca di terracotta da un vasaio e prendi con te alcuni degli anziani del popolo e degli anziani dei sacerdoti; (19:1).
rècati nella valle del figlio di Innom, che è all’ingresso della porta dei Vasai, e là proclama le parole che io ti dirò. (19:2).

Dirai così: “Ascoltate la parola del Signore, o re di Giuda e abitanti di Gerusalemme! Così parla il Signore degli eserciti, Dio d’Israele: ‘Ecco, io faccio venire sopra questo luogo una calamità che farà intronare gli orecchi di chi ne sentirà parlare. (19:3).

"Because the people have forsaken me and have profaned this place by making offerings in it to other gods whom neither they nor their fathers nor the kings of Judah have known; and because they have filled this place with the blood of innocents" (19:4),
"and have built the high places of Baal to burn their sons in the fire as olocaustos to Baal, which I did not command or decree, nor did it come into my mind" (19:5)—
Perciò, ecco, i giorni vengono’, dice il Signore, ‘in cui questo luogo non sarà più chiamato Tofet, né la valle del figlio di Innom, ma Valle del Massacro. (19:6).

Io renderò vani i disegni di Giuda e di Gerusalemme in questo luogo, farò in modo che costoro cadano per la spada davanti ai loro nemici e per mano di quelli che cercano la loro vita; darò i loro cadaveri in pasto agli uccelli del cielo e alle bestie della terra. (19:7).
"And I will make this city a horror, a thing to be hissed at. Everyone who passes by it will be horrified and will hiss because of all its wounds" (19:8).

Farò loro mangiare la carne dei propri figli e la carne delle proprie figlie; mangeranno la carne degli uni e degli altri, durante l’assedio e l’angoscia in cui li stringeranno i loro nemici e quelli che cercano la loro vita’”. (19:9).
Poi tu spezzerai la brocca in presenza di quegli uomini che saranno venuti con te e dirai loro: (19:10).

"and shall say to them, 'Thus says il SIGNORE of hosts: So will I break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter's vessel, so that it can never be mended. Men shall bury in Topheth because there will be no place else to bury'" (19:11).
"Thus will I do to this place," declares il SIGNORE, "and to its inhabitants, making this city like Topheth" (19:12).

Le case di Gerusalemme e le case dei re di Giuda saranno come il luogo di Tofet, immonde, tutte quelle case sui cui tetti essi hanno offerto profumi a tutto l’esercito del cielo e fatto libazioni ad altri dèi’”». (19:13).
Geremia tornò da Tofet, dove il Signore l’aveva mandato a profetizzare; si fermò nel cortile della casa del Signore e disse a tutto il popolo: (19:14).

"Thus says il SIGNORE of hosts, the God of Israel, behold, I am bringing upon this city and upon all its towns all the disaster that I have pronounced against it, because they have stiffened their neck, refusing to hear my words" (19:15).

stories.title: 🏺 Geremia 20
summaryBullets: Now Pashhur il sacerdote, figlio di Immer, who was chief officer in the house of il SIGNORE, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things (20:1).
Pascur percosse il profeta Geremia e lo mise nei ceppi nella prigione che era presso la porta superiore di Beniamino, nella casa del Signore. (20:2).
Il giorno seguente Pascur liberò Geremia dai ceppi. Geremia gli disse: «Il Signore non ti chiama più Pascur, ma Magor-Missabib. (20:3).

For thus says il SIGNORE: "Behold, I will make you a terror to yourself and to all your friends. They shall fall by the sword of their enemies while you look on. And I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon. He shall carry them captive to Babylon, and shall strike them down with the sword" (20:4).

Darò tutte le ricchezze di questa città, tutto il suo guadagno e tutte le sue cose preziose, darò tutti i tesori dei re di Giuda in mano dei loro nemici, che ne faranno loro preda, li piglieranno e li porteranno via a Babilonia. (20:5).
Tu, Pascur, e tutti quelli che abitano in casa tua, sarete deportati. Tu andrai a Babilonia e là morirai; là sarai sepolto con tutti i tuoi amici, ai quali hai profetizzato menzogne”». (20:6).
O LORD, you have deceived me, and I was deceived; you are stronger than I, and you have prevailed. I have become a laughingstock all the day; everyone mocks me (20:7).
For whenever I speak, I cry out, I shout, "Violence and destruction!" For the word of il SIGNORE has become for me a reproach and derision all day long (20:8).
If I say, "I will not mention him, or speak any more in his name," there is in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I am weary with holding it in, and I cannot (20:9).

For I hear many whispering. Terror is on every side! "Denounce him! Let us denounce him!" say all my close friends, watching for my fall. "Perhaps he will be deceived; then we can overcome him and take our revenge on him" (20:10).

But il SIGNORE is with me as a dread warrior; therefore my persecutors will stumble; they will not overcome me. They will be greatly shamed, for they will not succeed. Their eternal dishonor will never be forgotten (20:11).
O LORD of hosts, who tests the righteous, who sees the heart and the mind, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you have I committed my cause (20:12).
Cantate al Signore, lodate il Signore, perché egli libera il povero dalla mano dei malfattori! (20:13).
Cursed be the day on which I was born! The day when my mother bore me, let it not be blessed! (20:14).
Cursed be the man who brought the news to my father, "A son is born to you," making him very glad (20:15).
Pascur, figlio d’Immer, sacerdote e capo-sovrintendente della casa del Signore, udì Geremia che profetizzava queste cose. (20:16).
because he did not kill me in the womb; so my mother would have been my grave, and her womb forever great (20:17).
Why did I come out from the womb to see toil and sorrow, and spend my days in shame? (20:18).

stories.title: 🧭 Geremia 21
summaryBullets: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from il SIGNORE, when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur figlio di Malchiah and Zephaniah il sacerdote, figlio di Maaseiah, saying (21:1),

"Inquire of il SIGNORE for us, for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is making war against us. Perhaps il SIGNORE will deal with us according to all his wonderful deeds and will make him withdraw from us" (21:2).
Allora Geremia disse loro: «Direte così a Sedechia: (21:3).
"And I will bring them together into the midst of this city" (21:4).
"I myself will fight against you with outstretched hand and strong arm, in anger and in fury and in great wrath" (21:5).
"And I will strike down the inhabitants of this city, both man and beast. They shall die of a great pestilence" (21:6).

Poi’, dice il Signore, ‘io darò Sedechia, re di Giuda, e i suoi servitori, e il popolo, e coloro che in questa città saranno scampati alla peste, alla spada e alla fame, in mano di Nabucodonosor, re di Babilonia, in mano ai loro nemici, in mano di quelli che cercano la loro vita. Nabucodonosor li passerà a fil di spada; non li risparmierà e non avrà né pietà né compassione’”. (21:7).
A questo popolo dirai: “Così parla il Signore: ‘Ecco, io pongo davanti a voi la via della vita e la via della morte. (21:8).
Colui che rimarrà in questa città morirà di spada, di fame o di peste; ma chi ne uscirà per arrendersi ai Caldei che vi assediano vivrà, e avrà la vita come suo bottino. (21:9).
Io infatti volgo la mia faccia contro questa città per farle del male e non del bene’, dice il Signore; ‘essa sarà data in mano al re di Babilonia, ed egli la darà alle fiamme’”. (21:10).
«Alla casa dei re di Giuda di’: “Ascoltate la parola del Signore! (21:11).

Casa di Davide, così dice il Signore: Amministrate la giustizia fin dal mattino, liberate dalla mano dell’oppressore colui al quale è tolto il suo, affinché l’ira mia non divampi come fuoco e arda al punto che nessuno la possa spegnere, per la malvagità delle vostre azioni. (21:12).
Eccomi contro di te, o abitatrice della valle, roccia della pianura”, dice il Signore. “Voi dite: ‘Chi scenderà contro di noi? Chi potrà entrare nelle nostre abitazioni?’ (21:13).
"I will punish you according to the fruit of your deeds," declares il SIGNORE; "I will kindle a fire in her forest, and it shall devour all that is around her" (21:14).
